deities: Mahaganapati (Chatur-bhuja) — ancient 13th-century idol preserved beside a new idol consecrated in 1969

history.dynasty: Kadamba–Hoysala art influence on the ancient idol; relocations by the Goan Hindu community
history.period: Ancient idol 13th century CE; present Khandola temple with new idol consecrated 1969
history.summary: One of Goa's oldest Ganesha temples, with a unique dual-idol sanctum: the original temple at Ella was destroyed in the 13th-century Muslim invasion, the idols moving to Navelim, then Goltim, then the island of Divar. Portuguese missionaries pulled down the Divar temples in 1540 and the forced conversions of 1541–45 forced another move to Khandepar (whose laterite plinth ruins survive) and finally to Khandola. A new Shri Ganpati idol was consecrated here in 1969 while the ancient 13th-century Chatur-bhuja idol, showing Kadamba–Hoysala influence, is preserved alongside. name: Shree Mahaganapati Temple
town_description: Khandola is a small village near Marcela in Ponda taluka, North Goa, on NH 30 about 19 km from Panaji. Marcel lies close by, a town hosting more than 15 Hindu temples, and the area is known for its cluster of old shrines in the Ponda hinterland.
